model_output: The Nile is the longest river in the world, measuring approximately 6,853 kilometers (4,260 miles) in length. It is located in northeastern Africa and is the primary source of water for Egypt and Sudan. The Nile has two main tributaries: the White Nile and the Blue Nile. The White Nile originates in Lake Victoria in Uganda and flows through Tanzania, Rwanda, and Burundi, while the Blue Nile starts in Ethiopia and flows through Sudan and Egypt. The two rivers meet in Egypt and then flow into the Mediterranean Sea. The Nile has played a crucial role in the history and civilization of the region and continues to be an important source of water and transportation for the people living along its banks.
